data.name: Kafi
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word ‘kāfī’ meaning 'sufficient', 'complete', 'enough' or 'satisfying'. In Islamic history, it was the name of a renowned scholar, Al-Kāfī, known for his comprehensive collection of Hadith. This name evokes a sense of wholeness and self-sufficiency, inspiring a life of fulfillment and contentment.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the sufficiency of Allah in all aspects of life.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Kafi' holds a rich historical significance in Islamic culture. It is the name of Al-Kāfī, a prominent figure in Islamic history who is renowned for his extensive collection of Hadith, known as 'Al-Kāfī'. Al-Kāfī was born in the city of Kufa, Iraq, and was a scholar of great repute during the 9th century. His work, Al-Kāfī, is considered a highly authoritative source of Sunan (customs) and Sayings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Names inspired by scholars and their contributions to their respective fields have always been cherished in Islamic culture. Hence, the name Kafi imparts a sense of academic and intellectual exploration, while also promoting a deep reverence for the Prophet Muhammad's teachings and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Kafi' carries a profound spiritual meaning, symbolizing the concept of self-sufficiency, contentment, and fulfillment. The Arabic word 'kāfī' translates to 'sufficient', 'complete', 'enough', and 'satisfying'. From a spiritual standpoint, this name encourages individuals to strive towards attaining a state of self-sufficiency, both spiritually and materially. This sense of contentment and satisfaction comes from recognizing and appreciating the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us, and acknowledging our dependence on Him. In Islamic teachings, spiritual self-sufficiency is achieved through striving towards obedience to Allah, following Prophetic teachings, and maintaining a strong faith. Ultimately, the name Kafi serves as a constant reminder to remain grounded, self-reliant, and satisfied with life's blessings, while maintaining a strong connection with Allah.

historical_references.reference:
The book 'Kafi' by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, considered one of the Four Books of Shia Islam.
This work was compiled around 975 CE in the Buyid Empire in Iraq.
It is a collection of hadiths (sayings and acts of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions) and is a major source for Twelver Shia Islamic jurisprudence.
historical_references.context: Buyid Empire, Iraq, Collection of Hadiths, Twelver Shia Islamic Jurisprudence

historical_references.reference:
The term 'Kafi' also refers to a group of scholars known as the 'Kufan Scholars' who lived in the city of Kufa in the early Islamic period (650-750 CE).
These scholars were known for their rigorous adherence to Islamic law and their extensive knowledge of fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence).
They were also important transmitters and interpreters of hadiths.
historical_references.context: City of Kufa, Rigorous Adherence to Islamic Law, Extensive Knowledge of Fiqh, Transmitters and Interpreters of Hadiths
